body_markdown:
**Understanding the gap between consumers’ intentions and habits can help formulators identify meaningful opportunities for dishwashing innovation.**


Consumers expect more from[dishwashing products](https://www.iff.com/home-care/dish-wash/) . Powerful cleaning remains essential, but people also want sustainable formulations, shorter wash cycles, less prewashing and residue-free results.


Meeting all these priorities is not simple. What consumers say they want and the choices they make in their kitchens often tell different stories.


A recent[INFORM magazine](https://digitaledition.pub/wc/aocs/September-2026-Promo/) feature on IFF highlighted this disconnect. Although 80 per cent of consumers say sustainability is important, more than half still regularly prewash their dishes. Similarly, 75 per cent express interest in detergents designed for short cycles, yet standard, automatic and eco cycles remain the most common choices.


For detergent manufacturers and formulators, the gap between intention and action is more than a consumer contradiction. It is an opportunity to understand what prevents people from adopting new habits.


[INFORM Magazine Dish Feature](https://www.iff.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/INFORM-Magazine-Dish-Feature.pdf)[Download](https://www.iff.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/INFORM-Magazine-Dish-Feature.pdf)


## Performance Makes Behavior Change Possible


Consumers may want to use less water, reduce energy consumption or choose shorter wash cycles. But if those choices leave behind food residue, grease, or tea and coffee stains, reliability and convenience may take priority.


This creates a clear product development challenge. Solutions built around sustainability or convenience must still deliver the cleaning experience consumers expect. If consumers believe a[shorter or more resource-efficient cycle](https://www.iff.com/home-care/dish-wash/dishwashing-solutions/) compromises performance, they may return to familiar products and routines.


Formulators should not consider sustainability, convenience and performance in isolation. Successful innovation accounts for how these needs come together in real kitchens.


## Local Habits Shape Formulation Needs


Regional customs, generational expectations, available appliances and cleaning traditions all shape how people wash dishes. Detergent preferences also vary by market. Water hardness, cycle selection, temperature and common food soils can further affect performance.


As appliances advance, detergent formulations must evolve with them. Shorter cycles, lower water use, automatic dosing and new detergent formats create new demands for stability, compatibility and cleaning power. No single formulation or format can meet every market’s needs in the same way.


By understanding the local conditions, formulators can go beyond general consumer trends and develop solutions based on the[way dishes are really washed](https://www.iff.com/home-care/dish-wash/the-dish-issue-3/) .


## Innovation Begins With Real-World Understanding


Consumer insight is only most useful when it influences the development of products, which in turn involves linking the things that consumers value with the technical conditions that determine performance.


At IFF, researchers assess dishwashing enzymes and formulations across real-world variables. These include water hardness, detergent format, wash temperature, cycle length, appliance type and locally relevant food soils.
This practical approach helps researchers understand enzyme performance during controlled development and under the varied conditions found in households worldwide.


An innovation becomes meaningful when it fits consumers’ everyday realities. By examining the gap between what people believe and what they do, detergent brands can encourage new habits without asking consumers to sacrifice trusted performance.
